title: DS
content:
A data structure is a specialized format for organizing, processing, and storing data in a computer memory so it can be accessed and used efficiently.
Types of Data Structures
They are broadly divided into two main categories:
• Linear Data Structures: Elements are arranged sequentially or linearly, where each element is connected to its previous and next element.
	• Examples: Arrays (fixed-size index collections), Linked Lists (connected nodes via pointers), Stacks (Last-In, First-Out), and Queues (First-In, First-Out).
• Non-Linear Data Structures: Elements are not arranged sequentially; instead, they form a hierarchical or interconnected network.
	• Examples: Trees (hierarchical parent-child nodes) and Graphs (interconnected vertices and edges).
